title: The Sahityadarpana
author: vishvanatha-kaviraja
attributionNote: Written by Vishvanatha Kaviraja, a poet and scholar of Odisha, who wrote it as a manual for students of poetics.
description: The Sahityadarpana treats Sanskrit literary criticism as a single system in ten chapters: the definition of poetry and its language, the imagination the poet works with, the figures of speech with examples of each, the emotions and the states that carry them, the qualities and faults of a poem, the genres of drama and poem, and the conventions a reader is asked to accept.
historicalContext: Popular for its clarity and its balanced definition of poetry as language that conveys beauty and emotion, the work became the standard handbook of poetics in eastern India and is the account of Sanskrit literary theory most often read today.
availabilityNote: Complete: the ten chapters of the Sanskrit text as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
